summary: Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, where he was supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff and also studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. As a doctoral student at Temple University, he was supervised by Charles Wei-hsun Fu and studied under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Langdon Warner (1881–1955) worked in archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology after graduating from Harvard (A.B. ~1903). He directed the American School of Archaeology in China and the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and served as a Harvard lecturer (~1923–1950).

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and is attested as an Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at McGill in 2026.

Larry DeVries, an Indology and religious studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was attested at Langara College in 2005.

Lars Edman (1824–1921) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his doctorate at Uppsala University in 1857. He served there as a Docent in Oriental languages in 1857 and as Associate Professor of German and English (1863–1892).

Lars Fogelin specializes in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli and has held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (b. 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn. He is attested as a teacher at the University of Oslo in 2002.

Lars Nannestad Boisen (1803–1875) was a Danish scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Copenhagen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Bonn under scholars including Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, Christian Lassen, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Lata Chhatre is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Her academic career includes positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where she is attested as a Reader in Philosophy in 2009 and as Visiting Faculty in 2026.

Lata Deokar specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning her MA and PhD from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She worked at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2000–2012) and is attested as Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2026.

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Ganden Shartse (Geshe Lharampa, 1959) and Gyuto Monastery. He was Abbot of Ganden Shartse (~1976–1984) and a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia (1976).

Latika Lahiri (b. 1923) is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 and later held a post at the University of Delhi from around 1969 to 1988.

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under faculty including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Lozang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, and Tenzin Norbu.

Laura Massetti is a linguist and Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Cologne (2012–2016). She held research posts at Copenhagen, the Center for Hellenic Studies, and Oxford, and became a researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2022–2025).

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetology scholar who taught at Rutgers (attested 2003) and Indiana University Bloomington. Attested in 2026 at Columbia University, she directs the Modern Tibetan Studies Program and serves as Adjunct Assistant Professor in Tibetan Literature.

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) was a Tibetologist and archaeologist. Educated in medicine at Glasgow, he served in the Indian Medical Service and Army (~1879–1917), taught at Calcutta Medical College (1896), and became Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was an Oxford-educated scholar of art history, Sinology, and Japanology. He served at the British Museum (1893–1933), notably as Keeper of Oriental Prints and Drawings, and held visiting professorships at Harvard (1933–1934) and Athens (1940–1941).

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under teachers including Sangharakshita, Namkhai Norbu, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Chien Ming Chen. He served as abbot of Wat Buddha Dhamma beginning in 1978.

Laurent Van Cutsem specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from Université libre de Bruxelles, KU Leuven, and Ghent University (Doctorate, 2015–2023), where he was appointed Doctor-Assistant for 2023–2026.
